Rambaran vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: ?Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 36087 of 2022

Applicant :- Rambaran
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Kumar Yadav

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I,J.

Heard Sri Santosh Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Vinod Kumar Rai, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.
The instant application for bail has been moved on behalf of the applicant, Rambaran with the prayer to enlarge him on bail in F.I.R./ Case Crime No.138 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Mujariya, District Badaun, during pendency of the trial.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the first information report is based on false and fabricated facts.
The accused/ applicant is innocent who has been falsely implicated in this case because of the fact that the applicant happens to be husband of the deceased.
His further submission is that a false first information report came to be lodged against the present applicant in fact, he was not present in his house on the date of alleged incident.
There is no specific demand of dowry against the present applicant.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court to the statements of witnesses of Rambaran vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58883807/
1 fact, namely, PW-1, Natthu Lal, PW-2, Sarnish and PW-3, Dharmsheela, who have not supported the prosecution case and they have been declared hostile.
Therefore, the present applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Learned counsel for the applicant has also submitted that the accused/ applicant is languishing in jail since 12.10.2020 who has no previous criminal history.

His further submission is that in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and he will also fully cooperate with the trial court in getting the trial concluded expeditiously.
He has also submitted that the applicant will not intimidate or pressurize the witnesses or any other persons acquainted with the facts of the present case.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State has vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail by submitting that the accused/ applicant is named in the first information report.
The deceased was married to the present applicant three years prior to the death of the deceased in her matrimonial home.
His further submission is that the deceased has died in an unnatural manner in her matrimonial home within seven years of her marriage to the present applicant.

According to postmortem report,
the cause of death of the deceased is reported to be asphyxia due to strangulation.
There is one abrasion also found on the person of the deceased.
Therefore, the present applicant does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.

Having heard the learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and upon perusal of record, it transpires that the present applicant is named in the first information report who is the husband of the deceased.
The deceased was married to the present applicant three years prior to the date of the incident.
The applicant is said to have demanded Rs.2,00,000/- (rupees two lacs) in cash as dowry.
The deceased is said to have been treated with cruelty by all accused persons including the present applicant.
According to postmortem report, the cause of death of the deceased is reported to be asphyxia due to strangulation.
One antemortem injury, which is abrasion, has also been found on the person of the deceased.
The deceased has died in her matrimonial home within seven years of her marriage with the present applicant.

Thus, having regard to overall facts and circumstances of this case, the evidence collected during investigation against the applicant, seriousness of offence and the manner of commission of offence,
this Court does not find it a fit case for bail at this stage.
Accordingly, the instant application for bail is rejected.

However, keeping in view the fact that the accused/ applicant is languishing in jail since 12.10.2020,
the learned trial court is directed to proceed with the trial of the aforesaid case and conclude the same expeditiously and preferably within a period of six months from the date of production of certified copy of this order, in accordance with law, without granting any unnecessary adjournments to the parties, if there is no other legal impediment.

Rambaran vs State Of U.P. on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58883807/
2 S.S.P./ S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned are directed to ensure that witnesses are present on the date fixed so that their testimonies may be recorded without there being any hindrance.
Office is directed to communicate this order to the S.S.P/ S.P. and Joint Director Prosecution of the district concerned as well as trial court concerned separately for necessary compliance.

It is made clear that the trial of the aforesaid case shall be conducted without being influenced by any observation made herein above which are confined to the disposal of the instant application for bail.

(Ajai Kumar Srivastava-I, J.) Order Date :- 17.1.2023 cks/-
